analysis:
Examined the MTP upgrade file (head text) and the ModelLoading patch plus base text. Changes are small:
- ProviderLoop+MTPUpgrade.swift:127 adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) after isLoadingAny=true.
- ModelLoading ensureModelLoaded swaps autopilotAllowsModel for autopilotServesModel at the model-selection guard (~line 207).
- Same file adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) after isLoadingAny=true (~397) and a subject-scoped begin before modelsLoading.insert (~434).
- unloadModel calls reconcileAutopilotPlacements() after the slot is removed (~1148).
- evictableModelSlots also excludes slots that autopilotHoldsModel reports as held (~1303).

Security view:
- No change touches plaintext handling, encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization, the coordinator wire, or the SSD prefix cache (T-041 at-rest posture is unchanged).
- The tighter eviction and placement-hold logic restricts what can be evicted, so it adds no new disclosure path. It could affect availability if a hold is never released, but that is not evidenced here.
- The load-selection guard change (autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel) is the one item to verify. I cannot see either function's definition. If autopilotServesModel is stricter, it reduces unintended loads; if it is looser, it could admit loads outside Autopilot selection. The explicit command-owned load exception is unchanged.
- transitionGenerations.begin calls are added in the load paths shown. The matching finish/end calls are not visible in the supplied units, because the patch excerpt for ModelLoading is truncated and the base text ends at line 551. Unbalanced generations on early-throw paths, such as the slot-cap throw that resets isLoadingAny manually, could leave a transition marked open (availability or staleness of generation-gated checks). This is unverified.

The next pass should confirm three things: the semantics of autopilotServesModel, that transitionGenerations.begin is paired with release in every exit path (including the managedSuper and nativeLoad early returns and the MTP defer), and that reconcileAutopilotPlacements is safe to call re-entrantly.
